title: Bombieri-Vinogradov Theorem: Formalizability Assessment
description: Can the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem be formalized in Lean/Mathlib? This assesses the key analytic ingredient missing from the Maynard-Tao bounded prime gaps proof chain. BV states that primes are equidistributed in arithmetic progressions for almost all moduli up to √x. We formalize the theorem statement, define Chebyshev ψ functions, establish the level of distribution concept, and map the prerequisite roadmap (~12000 lines across 4 layers).

overview.historicalContext:
The Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem (1965) is one of the deepest results in analytic number theory. It shows that primes are equidistributed in arithmetic progressions 'on average' over moduli q up to √x, giving results of 'Riemann Hypothesis quality' without assuming RH. It was independently proved by Enrico Bombieri and Askold Ivanovich Vinogradov.

In 2013, Yitang Zhang used a variant of BV (with 'smooth moduli') as the key analytic input to prove bounded prime gaps. The Maynard-Tao improvement (2014) and Polymath 8b optimization used the full BV theorem to achieve the current record gap bound of 246.
overview.problemStatement:
**The Bombieri-Vinogradov Theorem**

For every A > 0, there exists B > 0 such that:

∑_{q ≤ Q} max_{gcd(a,q)=1} |ψ(x;q,a) - x/φ(q)| ≪ x/(log x)^A

where Q = √x/(log x)^B and ψ(x;q,a) = ∑_{n≤x, n≡a(q)} Λ(n).

**The Question:** Can this theorem be formalized in Lean/Mathlib?

**Answer:** Yes, in principle, but it requires ~12000 lines of infrastructure across 4 prerequisite layers. The critical missing piece is the Pólya-Vinogradov inequality for character sums.
overview.text: Assessment of Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem formalizability in Lean, with formal statement and prerequisite roadmap.
overview.proofStrategy:
1. Define Chebyshev ψ functions using Mathlib's von Mangoldt function
2. State BV as an axiom (proof requires ~12000 lines of missing infrastructure)
3. Define level of distribution and show BV gives θ = 1/2
4. Connect to Maynard-Tao sieve and Elliott-Halberstam conjecture
5. Map the 4-layer prerequisite roadmap with effort estimates
keyInsights: BV gives 'RH quality' results without assuming RH — primes equidistribute on average over moduli
The 4 prerequisite layers: character sums → analytic core → sieve methods → assembly (~12000 lines total)
Pólya-Vinogradov inequality is the single most impactful missing result for number theory in Mathlib
Formalizing BV would replace 1 of 3 axioms in the bounded prime gaps formalization
Mathlib already has ~70% of prerequisites (Dirichlet characters, L-functions, primes in AP)

sections.title: Chebyshev ψ Functions
sections.summary: Definitions of ψ(x), ψ(x;q,a), and π(x;q,a) using Mathlib's von Mangoldt function
sections.mathContext: $\psi(x) = \sum_{n \leq x} \Lambda(n)$, $\psi(x;q,a) = \sum_{n \leq x,\, n \equiv a(q)} \Lambda(n)$, expected main term $x/\varphi(q)$.

sections.title: The Bombieri-Vinogradov Theorem
sections.summary: Formal axiom statement of BV and immediate consequences (A=2 case)
sections.mathContext: BV: $\sum_{q \leq \sqrt{x}/(\log x)^B} \max_{\gcd(a,q)=1} |\psi(x;q,a) - x/\varphi(q)| \leq Cx/(\log x)^A$ for all $A > 0$. Achieves RH-quality equidistribution unconditionally.

sections.title: Connection to Maynard-Tao Sieve
sections.summary: Level of distribution θ=1/2, Elliott-Halberstam conjecture (θ→1 gives gap bound 12)
sections.mathContext: Level of distribution $\theta$: BV gives $\theta = 1/2$ unconditionally. EH conjecture: $\theta \to 1$. Under EH, Maynard-Tao gives gap bound 12 (vs 246 under BV).

sections.title: Prerequisite Roadmap
sections.summary: 4-layer roadmap: character sums (2000), analytic core (5000), sieves (3000), assembly (2000) = 12000 lines
sections.mathContext: Critical path: Pólya-Vinogradov ($|\sum \chi(n)| \leq \sqrt{q}\log q$) → Siegel-Walfisz → large sieve → Vaughan's identity → BV. Layer 1 alone enables ~30 other Mathlib PRs.

sections.title: Pólya-Vinogradov Inequality
sections.summary: Statement of the key missing Mathlib lemma and its role in the BV proof
sections.mathContext: Pólya-Vinogradov (1918): $|\sum_{n=M+1}^{M+N} \chi(n)| \leq \sqrt{q} \log q$ for non-principal $\chi \pmod{q}$, any $M, N$. The $\sqrt{q}\log q$ bound is independent of the interval length.

conclusion.summary: The Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem is formalizable in Lean 4 but requires approximately 12000 lines of infrastructure. The critical path runs through character sums (Pólya-Vinogradov) → zero-free regions → large sieve → proof assembly. Mathlib already provides ~70% of prerequisites.
conclusion.implications: Formalizing BV would be a landmark achievement in formal mathematics, replacing one of three axioms in the bounded prime gaps proof and establishing foundational infrastructure for all analytic number theory in Lean.
openQuestions: Can the Pólya-Vinogradov inequality be formalized as a Mathlib PR?
What is the minimal set of Mathlib additions needed for BV?
Could Zhang's 'BV with smooth moduli' variant be formalized with less infrastructure?
